1. Title

Exploration of AWS Cloud Computing Services and Complete Virtual Machine Lifecycle Management using Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2).

2. Aim

To study the architectural fundamentals of cloud computing (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS) and AWS core infrastructure services (EC2, S3, RDS, Lambda, ELB), and systematically configure, launch, monitor via Amazon CloudWatch, and safely terminate an Amazon EC2 Virtual Machine instance (t3.micro) under the AWS Free Tier.

3. Objectives

  • Understand Cloud Service Models: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Software as a Service (SaaS).
  • Explore Amazon Web Services core ecosystem: Amazon EC2, Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, Amazon RDS, Elastic Load Balancing (ELB), and Amazon ECS.
  • Study virtualization principles, hypervisors (Type 1 Bare-Metal vs Type 2 Hosted, and the AWS Nitro Hypervisor system).
  • Configure network firewall policies using AWS Security Groups (Port 22 SSH and Port 443 HTTPS).
  • Launch and verify a live running Linux virtual server (My-DevOps-EC2) in the Mumbai region (ap-south-1b).
  • Monitor compute telemetry (CPU utilization, network traffic, system and instance health checks) using Amazon CloudWatch.
  • Execute zero-cost termination and resource cleanup adhering to the AWS Free Tier.

8. Viva-Voce Examination Questions & Answers

Q1: What is the difference between AWS Security Groups and Network ACLs? Security Groups operate at the virtual network interface (ENI) level, are stateful (inbound return traffic automatically allowed), and evaluate permit rules only. Network ACLs operate at the subnet boundary, are stateless (inbound and outbound traffic must both be explicitly allowed), and evaluate ordered rule numbers.
Q2: Why is the t3.micro instance type selected for this DevOps laboratory? The t3.micro instance offers 2 vCPUs and 1 GiB memory on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, qualifying for 750 free hours per month under the AWS Free Tier, providing high burstable performance at zero financial cost.
Q3: What happens when an EC2 instance is Stopped vs Terminated? Stopping shuts down the virtual server operating system and halts per-second compute charges, but attached EBS storage volumes persist and accrue nominal storage fees. Terminating permanently destroys the virtual server and its root EBS volume, ensuring $0.00 ongoing charges.
Q4: What is the AWS Nitro System? AWS Nitro is a lightweight hypervisor architecture that offloads virtualization management (storage, network, security) to dedicated PCIe hardware cards, maximizing virtual machine CPU and memory performance.
Q5: How does Amazon CloudWatch assist in infrastructure reliability? CloudWatch automatically collects hypervisor metrics (CPU utilization, disk I/O, network traffic) every 5 minutes (or 1 minute in detailed monitoring) without requiring guest agent installation, enabling proactive alarming and autoscaling.
